title: VibeServe: can AI agents build bespoke LLM serving systems?
gist: A planner with long-term memory and an issue tracker drives an inner loop of implementer, accuracy judge and performance evaluator to build a whole serving stack for one model, one chip and one workload.
changes: A direct test of bespoke-per-workload: parity with general engines in the standard case, large wins only where the scenario is unusual. That is about where the value of specialisation should be expected to sit.
caveats: In the standard setting the result is a tie after 25 hours. The biggest win is against a baseline the authors had to patch to run. Single node, and it relies on a correctness checker the user supplies.

numbers.baseline: SGLang, patched by the authors to run

bears_on.note: Bespoke only pays where the workload is unusual. In the common case it ties.
Agents built a whole stack that matches a mature engine.
Removing the skills library lowered the ceiling. Here accumulated knowledge helped, the opposite of Together's finding.
